subject.title: Reduce tool schema token overhead (~3,500 tok/session)

question: Which default policy and implementation sequence should OpenClaw use to reduce model-facing tool-schema overhead without breaking cross-channel cron or isolated agents, provider schema contracts, or plugin/declarative tools?
rationale: The remaining work changes default prompt/schema visibility and crosses provider payloads, channel compatibility, Tool Search/deferred-schema semantics, plugin APIs, and possible config defaults, so maintainer intent is needed before implementation.

options.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
options.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

options.title: Defer To Narrower Issues
options.body: Close the umbrella and require all remaining work to happen only through focused issues such as Tooling-text skipping or deferred tool registration.

options.title: Adopt Aggressive Lazy Defaults
options.body: Make lazy or slim schemas the default now, accepting a broader compatibility and provider-contract review burden up front.

recommendation.title: Sequence Narrow Reductions
recommendation.body: Keep this tracker open and land small measured PRs for duplicate Tooling text, empty-tool definitions, safe message-schema pruning, shorter descriptions, and deferred or slim schema design.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest combined signal from recent prompt/runtime schema history and the existing issue sequencing discussion.
